title: Returning-Guest Relief on the Guest Service Fee of a Notice Charge
content:
# Returning-guest relief on the guest service fee of a notice charge — training Q&A

**The rule.** Guests who keep coming back get a returning-guest relief on the guest service fee of a notice charge on a cancelled reservation in the Stays (Guest Reservations) category, counted from the credits their Roamhaven Rewards ledger shows earned on completed stays in the last 24 calendar months: two or more such earnings relieve 25 percent of it; exactly one relieves 10 percent of it; none relieves nothing. Reliefs on that fee are added together, never relieve more than the whole fee, and are applied to the fee before it is rounded.

**What is counted?**
The credit-earning entries in the guest's Roamhaven Rewards ledger — credits earned on completed stays — posted in the last 24 calendar months. Each such earning counts once.

**How does the count turn into relief?**

| Credit earnings in the last 24 calendar months | Returning-guest relief |
|---|---|
| 0 | none |
| 1 | 10 percent |
| 2 | 25 percent |
| 3 or more | 25 percent |

**What happens when the fee also carries another relief?**
The percentages are added together and the total never exceeds the whole fee. With a returning-guest relief of 25 percent and another relief of 50 percent, 75 percent of the fee is relieved; with another relief of 100 percent, the total is held at the whole fee.

**When is the relief applied?**
Before the fee is rounded. A hypothetical unrounded fee of 133.335 with a 10 percent relief is 120.0015, which rounds half up to 120.00.

**Does an earning from 25 calendar months ago count?**
No; only earnings in the last 24 calendar months count.
